judged_text: SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction, where the previous code used the stored access token and refreshed only when needed. Every Salesforce-backed booking create/update/delete now pays an extra round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a credential DB write on the hot path; under booking load this multiplies Salesforce token-endpoint calls (rate-limit risk turns into failed bookings) and adds latency the previous path did not have.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then immediately does `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (see the newly added block starting with `const response = await fetch(...)` and the subsequent `await prisma.credential.update(...)`). There is no conditional check (e.g., token expiry) gating this refresh/update, so the finding’s claim about an unconditional extra network round-trip and DB write on the hot path is grounded in the diff. This is primarily a performance/rate-limit/latency concern rather than a definite correctness bug based solely on the diff.
